name: PurTox

lead:
PurTox is the name of a botulinum toxin type A product associated with Mentor Worldwide, a surgical-aesthetics company now part of Johnson and Johnson. Botulinum toxin products relax targeted muscles so the skin above them smooths, most often at the frown lines between the eyebrows.
Other botulinum toxins have approval for cosmetic use, such as Botox Cosmetic, approved by the FDA in 2002. Information on PurTox itself is sparse, and it is not among the brands listed on Wikipedia's botulinum toxin article.

paras: Cosmetic toxins in general are injected by trained clinicians into specific facial muscles; results usually appear in three to five days and last two to four months, sometimes longer, depending on product.

Class effects include bruising, headache, unintended weakness of nearby muscles such as eyelid drooping, and rarely spread of toxin effects, which led to FDA boxed warnings in 2009. Rx-only in regulated markets.

chain: Toxin blocks acetylcholine release in a targeted muscle
Frown lines and forehead creases soften
angle.text: Botulinum toxins smooth expression lines at the glabella and forehead and are also used to slim jaw muscle volume. The effect is temporary and repeated.

lead: PurTox is a botulinum toxin type A product from Mentor Worldwide, a Santa Barbara, California company that supplies surgical aesthetics products and became part of Johnson and Johnson in 2009 [1]. Botulinum toxin products work by blocking release of acetylcholine at nerve endings, producing temporary paralysis of the injected muscle, which smooths overlying lines [2].

Little published information on this specific product could be located, and it does not appear in the list of cosmetic toxin brands on Wikipedia's botulinum toxin article, which names Botox Cosmetic, Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau, Daxxify and Letybo [2]. This article therefore describes the product class.

paras: The first cosmetic observation came in 1987 when Richard Clark noticed improvement of a forehead asymmetry after facelift surgery; Carruthers published a glabellar-line study in 1992, and the FDA approved Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines in 2002 [2]. Smoothing usually shows by three to five days and peaks about a week later [2].

Reported effects include unintended paralysis of nearby facial muscles, headache, flu-like symptoms, bruising, allergic reactions and rare double vision; in 2009 the FDA announced boxed warnings about spread from the injection site [2].
No studies of PurTox specifically have been published.

timeline.event: FDA approves Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines (class milestone) [2].
Johnson and Johnson completes acquisition of Mentor [1].
